problem.explanation: For each outer employee, the correlated subquery finds MAX(salary) in that same department. Equality keeps all ties. A common mistake is calculating one company-wide maximum. RANK over department is a strong alternative for this greatest-per-group pattern.
hints: The comparison maximum must be calculated separately for each employee's department.
Use a correlated subquery whose department matches the outer row.
problem.reference_solution: SELECT name, department FROM employees e WHERE salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e.department) ORDER BY department, name
problem.statement_markdown: Return every employee tied for the highest salary in their department. Return name and department, sorted by department then name.
problem.title: Top earner per department
